# Run record — 296_R6FIX.29 (BL-116 invite over-redemption race)

- **Base:** `main` @ `26ba5bae` · **branch:** `stevevitali/r6fix-29-invite-race`
- Surfaced during the post-merge backlog audit (295_R6NOTE.4): the summary-section BL-116 row
  described a race the detailed sweep never covered. Verified live: the `used_count < max_uses`
  predicate sat in `cand` (snapshot read), so two concurrent different-user consumes could both
  insert and both increment — `used_count=2` on a single-use code. The 0016 comment's
  "conditional UPDATE" claim did not match the SQL.
- Fix: capacity guard moved onto the UPDATE (row lock + EPQ re-check); `ins` inserts only `from
  upd`; `not exists` preserves seat-free idempotent re-consume. Residual documented: concurrent
  same-user on multi-use over-counts by ≤1 — fails closed.
- **Tests:** invite.test.ts 7/7 (PGlite — sequential semantics + idempotent re-consume).
  Integration leg adds the real-Postgres race pin (10 rounds, used_count=1 + 1 redemption);
  `skipIf(!DATABASE_URL)` — runs on CI's postgres:16, skipped locally and reported as such.
- api + integration typecheck/lint clean.
- Folded dated closures: BL-119-sum (recipient PII — `main.ts:973` never logs it, `69c62e39`) and
  BL-120-sum (Resend `idempotencyKey` pass-through, `69c62e39`).
- Append-only vs `origin/main` · gitleaks — clean.
